name: smoke
notes: A smoke shape: tens of clients for a few minutes, to prove the harness end to end. It is never a baseline, and every report names its profile.
40 clients per instance: 32 agents (16 read · 8 write · 5 claim · 3 run) and 8 readers (6 tab · 2 browse).

COMPUTED by the resolver — offered ≤ 35 req/s per instance. targetRps 13 is about 0.37 × that offered figure, and 0.5 × the ~27 req/s the same clients offer when each call is counted once. It stays well under the bound so a healthy staging passes a smoke run.

ASSUMPTION — runs.agentSeconds 30, so a smoke run completes several run lifecycles inside its 3-minute window. That puts the /api/v1 rate per run token at about 0.45 req/s (27/min) of the 60/min budget.
ASSUMPTION — readers.holdSeconds 60, so each tab reconnects a few times in the window.
SHAPE — 2 agent workspaces (the smoke floor). 8 users, each a member of both with 4 tokens, mint 16 agents per role. The burst is 12 calls per agent, 2 agents, 30 s into the steady window.
TIMING — ramp 1 min, steady 3 min, ramp-down 15 s.
ASSUMPTION — roleSplit read 0.5 / write 0.25 / claim 0.15 / run 0.10 is the planner's decision for an agent-dominated mix (MOTIR-8678), not a reading of production traffic.
ASSUMPTION — toolWeights are chosen, not measured. transition_status carries weight 1 of 9 in the write role because each pick is TWO calls (todo → in_progress → todo).
ASSUMPTION — latencyAssumptionMs 200 (an MCP or /api/v1 call's p50) and readerLatencyAssumptionMs 300 (a page render's p50) feed only the offered-load arithmetic. The first smoke run reads both back.
ASSUMPTION — agentThinkSeconds 0.9 between a non-run agent's iterations, and readerBrowseThinkSeconds 5 between a browser's steps (±50 % jitter in the scenario).

COMPUTED — the offered load counts calls per iteration from the scenario code: read 1, write 1 + the transition share (1.11), claim 3 (claim, then release with update + transition, counted as always taking its card so the figure stays an upper bound). Run VUs come from requestsPerIteration. The burst and the per-frame workbench window reads are not in the steady figure.
ASSUMPTION — burst.retryAfterCapSeconds is the longest Retry-After any scenario waits before going on. It is the profile's only back-off cap, so every scenario receives it.
READING, NOT A THRESHOLD — proxy_shed (HTTP 503 per instance) is reported beside the verdict and judged by nothing.
